title: The rehearsal reader sees a ticket's landed commits and never raises landed work as a gap
intention: The rehearsal reader is told which of a ticket's commits have already landed, so it never raises work a landed commit already did as a gap.
why: After its kick-back, 41202d4c8d3b's rehearsal did not converge: 7 passes (about $3.9), and in 3 of them the reader raised work already landed at 9154af40 and fc17a873 as a gap, though the ticket's decisions named those commits. render() never tells the reader what landed, and prompt.md tells it every ticket is unbuilt. Ruled into this ticket by the peer's foreground calls F21 and F22 (/home/akien/.cairn/foreground-decisions.md lines 479 and 483), Akien's to overturn.
traces_to: Law 1 (the resolver is spent on the novel, not on re-deriving the settled): the reader re-derived landed work as open in 3 of 7 passes (k3 'write _sweep_order_problem helper and two test functions', k5 'Commit the build and verify', k7 'commit the build code to git' cannot_proceed), costing about $3.9 over 7 passes; and Akien's ruling open-a57cdd7cf3c1 that the reader must not take 'a million more passes to get something done'.
how:
In cairn/machines/rehearsal: render() appends a '# ALREADY LANDED' section carrying the ticket's workflow_and_state cursor and every commit in the repo whose message names the ticket id, one '<short hash> <subject>' line each, oldest first, or '(nothing landed for this ticket)'; prompt.md drops the false framing 'You are rehearsing a ticket BEFORE anyone builds it' and gains one rule: a step whose work a landed commit already did is builds_as_written, and no unlisted step is emitted for work a landed commit did. Two teeth in cairn/machines/rehearsal/proofs/test_rehearsal.py. Questions a Haiku-level builder would need, answered here: Where? cairn/machines/rehearsal/rehearsal.py, new module-level function landed(ticket: str, cursor: str, repo: Path) -> str, placed directly above render(). How? subprocess.run(['git', '-C', str(repo), 'log', '--reverse', '--format=%h %s', f'--grep={ticket}'], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True); lines = the stdout's non-empty lines. Returns '
# ALREADY LANDED

cursor: ' + cursor + '

' + ('
'.join(lines) if lines else '(nothing landed for this ticket)') + '
'. On subprocess.CalledProcessError or OSError returns '
# ALREADY LANDED

(landed commits could not be read: ' + str(exc) + ')
'. render(): after parts = [prompt(), ...ticket view...], parse the blob for workflow_and_state (json.loads; on failure or absence the cursor is '(no cursor)') and parts.append(landed(ticket, cursor, repo)); nothing else in render changes. prompt.md: replace the sentence 'You are rehearsing a ticket BEFORE anyone builds it, so that' with 'You are rehearsing a ticket so that' (the rest of that sentence unchanged), and add under ## Rules, directly after the whole-list rule: '- **Work that has ALREADY LANDED builds as written.** The ALREADY LANDED section lists the commits that name this ticket. A step whose work one of those commits already did is `builds_as_written` — there is nothing left to build — and you never emit an `unlisted:` step for work a landed commit did.' Proof: add T1 and T2 (names above) to proofs/test_rehearsal.py, under a PROVES entry for this ticket mapping '1' to T1 and '2' to T2; T1 builds its fixture repo with git init plus git -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t commit --allow-empty -m '<msg>' three times. The existing prompt tooth test_the_prompt_says_the_job_is_the_tree_and_cannot_proceed_is_legal_and_the_schema_mirrors_validate is left as is.
